questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Permutation Given Using Alternate Notation
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r}$ is given by

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\,.
$$

$P(7,4)$ means the same thing as ${}_{7}{P}_{4}.$ Using the usual formula for ${}_{n}{P}_{r},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(7,4) & =\frac{7!}{(7-4)!} \\  & =\frac{7!}{3!} \\  & =\frac{7\cdot 6\cdot 5\cdot 4\cdot \cancel{3!}}{\cancel{3!}} \\  & =840.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten
questions.problem: Cheryl holds a bag of $40$ marbles, each one with a slightly different size or color. If she picks $5$ of them out one at a time and lines up in a row, how many different lines of $5$ marbles are possible?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $40$ marbles to choose from, so $n=40.$ We want to select $5$ of those marbles for the line, so we have $r=5.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to line up $5$ marbles is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{40}{P}_{5} & =\frac{40!}{(40-5)!} \\  & =\frac{40!}{35!} \\  & =\frac{40\cdot 39\cdot 38\cdot 37\cdot 36\cdot \cancel{35!}}{\cancel{35!}} \\  & =40\cdot 39\cdot 38\cdot 37\cdot 36 \\  & =78\,960\,960.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
questions.problem: Victoria has the $4$ playing cards: the ace of clubs, the ace of diamonds, the ace of hearts, and the ace of spades. She takes one card and places it in front of her. She then does the same with another card. In how many different ways can she choose a sequence of $2$ cards like this?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $4$ cards, so $n=4.$ We want to select $2$ of those cards to make a sequence of $2$ cards, so we have $r=2.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to choose the cards is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{4}{P}_{2} & =\frac{4!}{(4-2)!} \\  & =\frac{4!}{2!} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 3\cdot \cancel{2!}}{\cancel{2!}} \\  & =4\cdot 3 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group of at Least Ten
questions.problem: Erik has an encyclopedia with $24$ tomes and is selecting $3$ tomes to read first, second, and third. How many different choices does Erik have?
questions.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $24$ tomes to choose from, so $n=24.$ We want to select $3$ of those tomes for Erik to read, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of choices Erik has is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{24}{P}_{3} & =\frac{24!}{(24-3)!} \\  & =\frac{24!}{21!} \\  & =\frac{24\cdot 23\cdot 22\cdot \cancel{21!}}{\cancel{21!}} \\  & =24\cdot 23\cdot 22 \\  & =12\,144.\end{aligned}
$$
